scope_line: Scope: the hermes-agent repository (agent loop, tools, skills, curator, approvals, gateway, MCP and ACP servers, desktop and web, CI) plus the first-party hermes-agent-self-evolution repository (DSPy and GEPA skill optimisation). Nous Portal and hosted services are out of scope.

MAL-01.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-02.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-03.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-04.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-05.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-06.evidence: Typed tool schemas (model_tools.py, toolsets.py) served over MCP (mcp_serve.py) and the Agent Client Protocol (acp_adapter); no OpenAPI description of the serve API and no dry-run.

MAL-07.evidence: CLI, TUI, desktop and web layouts are code; persona text (SOUL.md) is data but is not layout.

MAL-08.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD views (fixed per-archetype rule).

MAL-09.evidence: UI strings externalised in locales/ and translated READMEs; themes are engineer-managed.

MAL-10.evidence: Cron jobs are defined in natural language or the CLI and run agent tasks on schedules (cron/); plugin hooks add behaviour; there is no general condition and action engine.

MAL-11.evidence: Gateway adapters receive platform and webhook events; the MCP server lets clients poll live events (mcp_serve.py); no retry or replay for outbound subscribers.

MAL-12.evidence: Plugins register hooks that run in-process without a sandbox (plugins/); the agent's own commands can run in Docker, SSH or remote sandbox backends with guards (tools/terminal_tool_backends.py, terminal_tool_guards.py).

GOV-01.evidence: No automated accessibility scanning found for the TUI, desktop or web interfaces.

GOV-02.evidence: Every skill mutation by any actor is appended to a JSONL ledger with content-addressed before and after snapshots (tools/skill_ledger.py); staged approvals are recorded; sessions are stored in SQLite. Configuration and memory changes are not in the ledger.
GOV-02.alt_note: Skills are the main definition surface and are fully audited with approvals.

GOV-03.evidence: Session export and import (hermes_state_portability.py) and user-editable memory files; data stays on the user's machine; not driven by tags.

GOV-04.evidence: Command scanning with tirith and dangerous-command approvals with an LLM risk classifier and floors (tools/approval_smart.py, approval_floors.py); skill security scans and AST audits before install or write (tools/skills_guard.py, skills_ast_audit.py); OSV and supply-chain scans in CI (.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml, supply-chain-audit.yml).

GOV-05.evidence: Skills have a per-mutation ledger with single-edit rollback that fails closed (tools/skill_ledger.py) and curator archives are restorable, but configuration has only point-in-time copies on some writes (hermes_cli/config_backups.py) and memory files have no history. Under the inventory rule a 3 needs every default surface at 3.

GOV-06.evidence: By default, skill and memory writes apply directly and are ledgered. With skills.write_approval or memory.write_approval on, writes are staged with a gist and applied through /skills approve (tools/write_approval.py:73-189); the self-evolution repo proposes evaluated skill variants as pull requests.

GOV-07.evidence: By default only protected instruction files always need a human (cli-config.yaml.example:573-576); skill and memory gates default to off (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1320). With them on, each change class has its own gate.

GOV-08.evidence: Numbered configuration migrations run on update (hermes_cli/config_migrations.py:379-397); bundled-skill sync updates shipped skills without overwriting user copies (tools/skills_sync*.py); skills follow the agentskills.io specification.

ARC-01.rationale: Agent runtime: generic-store query performance (fixed per-archetype rule).

ARC-05.rationale: Scope fact multi_tenant is false: One user per installation; profiles are separate homes, not tenants.

ARC-06.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A local single-user agent; the gateway relays messaging platforms for the same user.

DEL-02.evidence: Python agent, gateway, desktop, web and sandbox images are separate artifacts built from one repository (Dockerfile, .github/workflows/sandbox-image.yml, desktop-bundled-release.yml).

DEL-03.evidence: Import guards in CI (.github/workflows/lazy-deps-guard.yml, case-collision-check.yml); no architectural boundary lint.

DEL-05.evidence: Python, JavaScript and Rust tests, lint, Nix, OSV, supply-chain, desktop E2E and install E2E run in CI with no draft filter (.github/workflows/tests.yml, js-tests.yml, rust-tests.yml, e2e-desktop.yml); no accessibility check.
DEL-05.alt_note: Every change class except accessibility is checked.

MAL-13.evidence: Declarative skills (SKILL.md), Python plugins with hooks, MCP servers, providers and a plugin catalogue with hundreds of entries (plugin-catalog/, skills/, optional-skills/, optional-mcps/).
MAL-13.alt_note: A versioned registry and hub exist.

MAL-14.evidence: Hub skills are scanned and installed only after confirmation (tools/skills_hub_install.py, skills_guard.py); plugins run with full trust; commands can be sent to sandbox backends.
MAL-14.alt_note: Scanned skills plus sandboxed command backends isolate most third-party and AI-written code.

MAL-15.evidence: Skill linter (tools/skill_linter.py), curator dry-run (hermes curator run --dry-run), logs (hermes_logging.py) and local iteration against the user's own profile.

MAL-19.evidence: MCP server exposing conversation, messaging, event and approval tools (mcp_serve.py) and an ACP adapter for editors (acp_adapter/); typed tool registry (model_tools.py). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: The MCP surface covers messaging, not the full capability set.
MAL-19.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

ai.evidence: MCP server and ACP adapter (mcp_serve.py, acp_adapter).

MAL-20.evidence: Users complete tasks conversationally across CLI, desktop and messaging platforms with tool actions; users author skills, memory and cron jobs in natural language, with staged approvals as preview when enabled; evaluation probes (evals/) and GEPA evaluation datasets.
MAL-20.alt_note: Almost every capability is reachable conversationally.

ai.evidence: Model-backed conversation across platforms; skills and memory authored in natural language.

GOV-09.evidence: Dangerous-command approvals with LLM risk classification and floors, tirith scanning, sandbox backends, subagent auto-deny and session audit; commands otherwise run with the user's ambient authority; no idempotency keys.
GOV-09.alt_note: Per-action risk classification and approval previews are level 3 and 4 features.

ai.evidence: Dangerous commands need approval with LLM risk classification; the agent acts with the user's authority.

MAL-16.evidence: One provider layer maps many model vendors onto a canonical chat interface (providers/, agent/*_adapter.py), and one gateway maps Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp and other platforms onto a canonical conversation model (gateway/).

MAL-17.evidence: Plugin catalogue entries, provider adapters, platform adapters and MCP servers cover auth, messaging and lifecycle; skill hub sources include official, GitHub, ClawHub and skills.sh (tools/skills_hub_*.py).

MAL-18.evidence: Standard protocols (MCP, ACP, OpenAI-compatible APIs) and versioned configuration; no deprecation windows.

EXP-01.evidence: Kernel of sessions (conversation), gateway platforms (channel), profiles (identity), approvals (permission), cron and delegation (workflow), and skills and files (content); no domain nouns.

EXP-02.evidence: Many domains ship as skill bundles on an unchanged kernel (skills/, optional-skills/), and the agent creates new domain skills itself. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: If skills are judged too small to count as domains.
EXP-02.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 4 on the evidence above.

EXP-03.evidence: Skills are versionable, installable bundles under the agentskills.io specification, installed from the hub with scanning and synced on update.
EXP-03.alt_note: Bundles are composable (curator umbrella skills), upgradeable and AI-assembled.

LRN-01.evidence: The session database with full-text search is available to the agent in real time (hermes_state_fts.py, hermes_state_search.py); every skill gets view, use and patch counts automatically (tools/skill_usage.py).
LRN-01.alt_note: Per-definition instrumentation is added automatically for every skill.

LRN-02.evidence: Every skill has view, use and patch counts linked to it (tools/skill_usage.py), and the curator triages skills into active, stale and archived (website/docs/user-guide/features/curator.md). Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: Usage counts are not versioned per skill revision.
LRN-02.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

LRN-04.evidence: Session search over the agent's own history; the self-evolution repo builds evaluation datasets from Hermes, Claude Code and Copilot session histories (README, --eval-source sessiondb). No continuous mining in the product.

LRN-06.evidence: After each turn a background fork proposes skill and memory updates grounded in the conversation (agent/background_review.py); GEPA ranks skill variants on a Pareto front with evaluation evidence (self-evolution repo). Covers skills only.
LRN-06.alt_note: Ranked, evidence-backed proposals with expected impact exist for the agent's main behaviour surface.

ai.evidence: A background fork proposes skill and memory updates from the conversation.

DEL-04.evidence: The background review is an autonomous authoring lane that applies skill and memory changes every turn (agent/background_review.py); GEPA improvements reach every user through upstream pull requests. Scored at the lower reading under rule 11 because: The cross-user path depends on an offline companion tool.
DEL-04.alt_note: The September v0.3 pass scored 3 on the evidence above.

ai.evidence: Background review is a model lane that applies skill and memory changes.

LRN-09.evidence: The curator keeps, marks stale or archives skills from measured usage over fixed windows (14 and 30 days, website/docs/user-guide/features/curator.md); GEPA compares variants against the baseline skill before proposing. Nothing measures the outcome of an applied skill in use.
LRN-09.alt_note: The curator records a metric, window and explicit keep or archive decision per skill.

LRN-10.evidence: The checks that govern change are code: skill scans, AST audit and linter (tools/skills_guard.py, skills_ast_audit.py, skill_linter.py), the memory scan and write gates (tools/memory_tool.py) and the optimiser's fixed constraint gates (hermes-agent-self-evolution evolution/core/constraints.py:24-174). People improve evaluation material by hand outside the product: regression probes in evals/ (69 entries) are written by engineers, and the optimiser builds an evaluation set per run from synthetic cases, mined session history or hand-curated golden sets (evolution/core/dataset_builder.py, external_importers.py) when a person runs it. Nothing records a wrong pass against the check that missed it, evaluation sets are not versioned through the product's change path, and policy changes do not cite results.

DEL-06.evidence: Version reporting and state health checks (hermes_state_health.py) and a configuration display; no machine-readable deployed-configuration endpoint.

DEL-07.evidence: Nix flake and lock files reproduce the environment (flake.nix, uv.lock); install E2E jobs build fresh environments per run.
DEL-07.alt_note: Reproducible environments are built per change in CI.

DEL-08.evidence: Behaviour probes (evals/), desktop and install E2E suites; no changed-path map or adoption instrumentation at ship.

LRN-07.evidence: background_review is enabled by default (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:814): after turns, a forked agent decides whether to save or update skills and memory (agent/background_review.py).
LRN-07.alt_note: The curator's consolidation learns which skills stick, but only when enabled.

ai.evidence: Model reflection after turns writes skills and memory by default.

LRN-08.evidence: Re-checked for v0.7 under the tightened boundary; unchanged. Skill writes by the agent and the background review pass security scans, AST audits and a linter (tools/skills_guard.py, skills_ast_audit.py, skill_linter.py), and memory writes are scanned and destructive background deletes gated (tools/memory_tool.py:44, 84-205). The first-party optimiser evaluates variants against the baseline skill on a holdout set before proposing, when a person runs it (hermes-agent-self-evolution evolution/skills/evolve_skill.py:185-210).

ai.evidence: AI-written skills pass scans, AST audits and a linter.

ARC-02.evidence: The state database migrates forward on start (hermes_state_schema.py) and hermes update takes a pre-update snapshot it restores when an update fails (hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:109-110), with migration tests (tests/hermes_state).
ARC-02.alt_note: Snapshot restore is a tested rollback path.

ARC-08.evidence: Fallback providers and credential pools take over when a primary model fails (agent/agent_init.py, tests/agent/test_restore_primary_pool_reselect.py); tool and MCP failures are contained to the turn. Plugins and gateway platforms have no breakers, so a 3 is not defensible under the inventory rule.

ai.evidence: Fallback providers and credential pools contain provider failure, with tests.

ARC-09.evidence: hermes backup and import cover the home directory: the sessions database (snapshotted with sqlite3.backup), skills, memory, configuration and secrets such as .env, auth.json and the vault (hermes_cli/backup.py:117-161), with pre-update backups and round-trip tests (tests/hermes_cli/test_backup*.py). No recovery objectives are stated (level 4). Scheduled work: cron/jobs.json is in every backup and jobs lost during an update are restored automatically (hermes_cli/backup.py:1059, 1600-1665); hermes cron list shows each job's next run (hermes_cli/cron.py:125); jobs run under their own profile (cron/jobs.py:64-68); a pre-run check, on by default, blocks and alerts on jobs whose provider key, delivery target or skills no longer resolve (cron/scheduler_preflight.py:80-90, 387), with tests (tests/cron/test_preflight_credential_verdict_names_home.py).

DEL-01.evidence: Requests are chat turns; the agent can create a skill when asked, without a specification step.
DEL-01.alt_note: Skill creation on request records name and description.

ai.alt_note: Skill creation records name and description.

DEL-09.evidence: Update channels let an installation take canary builds before stable (hermes_cli/update_channel.py); skill and memory changes are not staged.

DEL-10.evidence: Background review and individual skills can be switched off in configuration at runtime; curator archives remove skills without a release.

DEL-11.evidence: Two code paths. Product releases: hermes update rolls back a pulled tree that fails a syntax check and restores the state snapshot on failure (hermes_cli/update_cmd.py:840-870); there is no one-step rollback to the previous release. Code the agent writes into skills: every skill mutation, supporting files included, is ledgered with before and after snapshots and can be rolled back one entry at a time with `hermes curator rollback`, failing closed (tools/skill_ledger.py:569, hermes_cli/curator.py:509). Re-checked for v0.7 after the code_release_path grounds changed; score unchanged.

LRN-03.evidence: Background review sees corrections and failures in recent turns, and evals record failures found in use (evals/).

LRN-05.evidence: hermes doctor diagnoses setup problems and cron error diagnostics attach context to failing jobs (hermes_cli/main.py:2567).

ai.evidence: The agent explains errors when asked; hermes doctor is rule-based.

GOV-10.evidence: Protected instruction files always need a person, and skill writes pass scans and an AST audit (tools/skills_guard.py); there is no declared scope or rate limit for background changes.

ai.evidence: Protected files and write scans; no declared scope or rate limit.

GOV-11.evidence: The skill ledger records the actor of every mutation (tools/skill_ledger.py:54-68) and the skills guard scans writes for injection and exfiltration patterns (tools/skills_guard.py:42-140); session content can still drive an automatically applied skill change.
GOV-11.alt_note: Provenance and injection scanning are both present.

ai.evidence: Ledger actor and injection scans on skill writes.

EXP-04.evidence: Unserved requests stay in session history; nothing records them as unmet demand.

EXP-05.evidence: Background review creates skills for tasks it has just done; it does not propose capabilities nobody has used yet.

ai.evidence: Creates skills for tasks it has done; no unprompted proposals.

EXP-06.evidence: New skills apply to the whole installation at once.

ARC-03.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A local single-user agent; the gateway relays messaging platforms for the same user.

ARC-04.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A local single-user agent; the gateway relays messaging platforms for the same user.

ARC-07.rationale: Scope fact hosted_service is false: A local single-user agent; the gateway relays messaging platforms for the same user.

AIR-01.evidence: Fallback providers and credential pools take over when a primary model fails, with tests (agent/agent_init.py, tests/agent/test_restore_primary_pool_reselect.py).

AIR-02.evidence: Usage and pricing per turn and per account are tracked (agent/usage_pricing.py, turn_usage.py, billing_usage.py) and iterations are budgeted (agent/iteration_budget.py); no spend limit per user.
AIR-02.alt_note: Iteration budgets bound usage per task.

AIR-03.evidence: Session search over full-text indexes, memory and skills injected into context, with memory provider plugins (hermes_state_fts.py, plugins).

AIR-04.evidence: A single-user agent acting with the user's own permissions; the gateway accepts only paired users, profiles isolate homes, and dangerous commands need approval (tools/approval_smart.py), with security tests (tests/security).

AIR-05.evidence: Regression probes named after failures found in use (evals/) and GEPA skill evaluation in the companion repository, run on request.

AIR-06.evidence: Evaluations are not part of CI.

AIR-07.evidence: Sessions record every message, tool call and model in the state database, with trajectories and trace upload (agent/trajectory.py, trace_upload.py, hermes_state_*.py), queryable through hermes sessions and insights.

AIR-08.evidence: Skill usage counts feed the curator; no quality or feedback monitoring of the agent's answers.

limits: Repository evidence only. The self-evolution repository's last commit is 2026-06-17, and only phase 1 (skills) is implemented; phases 2 and 3 were not scored. No live runs were performed, so the effects of background review and the curator are read from code and documentation. Single rater.
reading: **SAL 1.** Issue → Fix reaches L2: background review turns corrections and failures into skill and memory changes by default (LRN-07 3), and hermes doctor diagnoses setup problems (LRN-05 2). Request → Release stops at L1 because requests are chat turns with no specification step (DEL-01 1); raising that one criterion would lift the headline. **Controls:** backup and restore cover every surface including secrets and are tested (ARC-09 3), but configuration and memory lack the rollback skills have (GOV-05 2, inventory) and background changes have no declared scope or rate limit (GOV-10 2).

persistent_data.evidence: Sessions in SQLite, plus skills, memory and configuration under HERMES_HOME.

schema_changes.evidence: The state database is versioned and migrated on start (hermes_state_schema.py, SCHEMA_VERSION).

multi_tenant.evidence: Re-checked under the v0.7 definition: one person per installation; profiles are separate homes of the same person, which the definition excludes, and the gateway serves only that person's paired accounts. No groups that administer themselves.

hosted_service.evidence: A local single-user agent; the gateway relays messaging platforms for the same user.

machine_actions.evidence: The agent's tools change its own skills, memory and configuration, and the MCP and ACP servers expose it to other clients (mcp_serve.py, acp_adapter).

agent_mutations.evidence: The background review writes skills and memory after turns (agent/background_review.py); the skill manager tool creates and edits skills and their supporting files (tools/skill_manager_tool.py), and the memory tool writes MEMORY.md and USER.md (tools/memory_tool.py).

evolution_auto_apply.evidence: background_review is on by default and skill and memory write approvals default to off (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:814, 1320).

definition_change_path.evidence: Skills, memory, prompts and configuration are its definitions.

code_release_path.evidence: Kept true for v0.7 on different grounds. The September reason does not meet the tightened definition: the self-evolution optimiser produces SKILL.md text, a declarative definition, and writes it to an output folder for a person to submit (hermes-agent-self-evolution evolution/skills/evolve_skill.py:180-285); no code opens a pull request. But the agent writes scripts into skills it creates (tools/skill_manager_tool.py:114, ALLOWED_SUBDIRS includes scripts) and runs them when it later uses the skill; the product audits that code with an AST audit (tools/skills_ast_audit.py). That is code the product's own AI writes and activates.

ai_features.evidence: The product is an LLM agent.

ai_data_access.evidence: Reads the user's files, sessions, memory and skills (session search, memory providers).

ai_actions.evidence: Runs commands, edits files and sends messages on the user's behalf (tools/).

change_kinds.name: What the agent knows how to do (skills)
change_kinds.evidence: The background review drafts and writes skills after turns, on by default (agent/background_review.py; hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:814); with skills.write_approval on, writes are staged for /skills approve (tools/write_approval.py:73-189). People install hub skills after a scan (tools/skills_hub_install.py). Undo: every mutation is ledgered and `hermes curator rollback` reverts one entry, failing closed (tools/skill_ledger.py:569, hermes_cli/curator.py:509). Reach 2 rests on DEL-04 2; nothing builds, checks and stages a skill change end to end for approval by default.

change_kinds.name: What the agent remembers and how it presents itself
change_kinds.evidence: The memory tool and the background review write MEMORY.md and USER.md, with scans and delete gates (tools/memory_tool.py); SOUL.md and other protected instruction files need a person (cli-config.yaml.example:573-576). No supported undo: memory files keep no history (GOV-05 inventory: memory 1). Reach 0 because the path has no undo. Undo rule used in this field test: a kind has undo when the product keeps the earlier version, or when the change is a selection, toggle or add-and-remove that the same supported path reverses exactly; free-text or multi-field edits with no kept version have none.

change_kinds.name: Which models and providers it uses, and its settings
change_kinds.evidence: Models and providers are selected with `hermes model` and settings changed with `hermes config` and the setup flows (hermes_cli/config_migrations.py for upgrades). Undo is selecting the previous model or value again; some writes keep point-in-time copies used only for automatic recovery (hermes_cli/config_backups.py:45-90), and there is no command to list or restore an earlier version, so larger edits have no undo. Undo rule used in this field test: a kind has undo when the product keeps the earlier version, or when the change is a selection, toggle or add-and-remove that the same supported path reverses exactly; free-text or multi-field edits with no kept version have none.

change_kinds.name: Scheduled and recurring tasks
change_kinds.evidence: Jobs are created, paused and removed in natural language through the cronjob_manage tool, with prompt scanning (tools/cronjob_tools.py, cronjob_prompt_scan.py), or with `hermes cron` (hermes_cli/cron.py). Undo is pausing or removing the job; edits keep no earlier version.

change_kinds.name: Which tools it may use and what needs approval
change_kinds.evidence: Toolsets and MCP tools are enabled and disabled with `hermes tools` (hermes_cli/tools_config.py:35, tools_disable_enable_command), and approval behaviour is configuration (tools/approval_smart.py). Toggles are undone by toggling back; approval settings keep no earlier version (GOV-05 inventory: configuration 2). Undo rule used in this field test: a kind has undo when the product keeps the earlier version, or when the change is a selection, toggle or add-and-remove that the same supported path reverses exactly; free-text or multi-field edits with no kept version have none.

change_kinds.name: Add-ons for new platforms, providers and tools
change_kinds.evidence: `hermes plugins install` from the catalogue and `hermes plugins remove|uninstall` (hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py:982-984, plugins_cmd_install.py, plugins_cmd_remove.py), with a plugin ledger (plugins_ledger.py). Undo is removal.

ai_delivery.evidence: AGENTS.md at the repository root. No agent steps in CI: the workflows that mention Anthropic or Claude are provider tests and a contributor allowlist (.github/workflows/contributor-check.yml:47, live-providers.yml). The self-evolution companion is scored as part of the product, not as delivery tooling.
ai_delivery.note: Engineers use AI coding agents (AGENTS.md); instruction files alone do not count under rule 12, and no delivery framework is installed.

request.searched: Both repositories at the pinned commits: no operating records of requested skills or configuration changes going through the loop in a real installation (skill ledgers live in each user's HERMES_HOME).

fix.searched: Both repositories: no background-review or skill-ledger records from a real installation; the self-evolution reports/phase1_validation_report.pdf is a validation study, not operating records of the product's own loop.

expansion.searched: Both repositories: no records of new capabilities proposed and launched.

confidence_note: Confidence for criteria this migration did not change was assigned at migration to v0.7 from the recorded evidence (high where it names the code path and its tests or exact lines, medium where it names files but not every path, low where it rests on an absence claim or general description); criteria re-read for v0.7 carry the confidence of that re-reading.
